# 504 synthetic actual-component candidate

This is a synthetic component qualifier. Each result applies only to the recorded source and checks; it does not qualify a production deployment. Root generates the private synthetic credentials and runs the reviewed source through the existing owned runner and exec-only adapter.

The nine 0600 runtime files in `--material` are exactly `ca.pem`, `product.pem`, `product.key`, `export.pem`, `export.key`, `server.pem`, `server.key`, `evidence.pem`, and `evidence.key`; the directory and its protected parent chain must satisfy the private-file checks. Server certificates need the fixed DNS names in the task contract. The synthetic issuer input file passed as `--payload` is host-only and must be 0600, single-link, under a protected 0700 directory. It contains `R5I1`, a four-byte big-endian JSON length, and exactly that many canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes. The closed, sorted keys are `backend_cert`, `backend_key`, `gateway_cert`, `gateway_key`, `ingress_cert`, `ingress_key`, `seed`; values are canonical padded base64 of synthetic material, and `seed` decodes to exactly 32 bytes. Entire framed input is bounded to 65536 bytes. Generate it without printing or placing any contents in command-line arguments, environment, logs or receipts.

The owned runner launches `exec_input.py` as the fixed helper. It checks a pinned Docker executable/digest and endpoint, an empty private Docker config, the full CID, and the protected input's exact length, hash and file identity. It duplicates that same open input descriptor to stdin, closes inherited descriptors above 2, and execs only `docker --host <fixed-socket> start --attach --interactive <full-CID>`. The container is created with `OpenStdin=true`, `Tty=false`, and `StdinOnce=true`; its fixed shell command duplicates stdin to fd 3 and closes fd 0 before execing the Node parent. This one-shot attach closes container stdin after the attached client disconnects; it does not support reconnecting to deliver a second input. The parent reads the exact bounded frame from its owned fd 3 and awaits that stream's close before spawning the fixed 504 proxy. The synthetic peer keys and seed are never mounted into the container or passed to the child as environment or arguments. Normal runtime material remains in the nine required read-only mounts. File checks assume the protected host and no malicious concurrent same-UID writer; they are not immutable-input or host-attestation guarantees.

The helper starts loopback-only synthetic mTLS backend and ACK endpoints, handles CBP2/CLB2/CQP2/CRP2/CLR2, and submits one actual HTTPS request to Node-RED. The prepared checks require a private receiver fact matching that request's binding and a root in the exact producer batch that received the validated synthetic duplicate ACK. The first receiver ACK is lost; the retry must have identical bytes and one logical server-side assignment. Actual wrong-role mTLS requests use those previously valid payloads and must receive an empty 403 without acceptance. The outbox stays private: observing the server-side retry does not directly prove that the client parsed the second receipt or drained its ticket.

Output is limited to closed phase/check labels. Synthetic acknowledgements do not prove SQL20 commit, SQL28/29 enrollment or admission, trusted issuer/deployment authority, real gateway semantics, or a durable edge. Scrub, replay, current-authority, instance binding and platform coverage require their separately scoped evidence; no receipt may infer them from an ordinary producer root. The fixed child environment has exactly eleven keys, including `UV_USE_IO_URING=0` on both architectures; other keys or values remain rejected.

The runner snapshots the protected socket and its ancestor identities before its first Docker command, verifies that same snapshot before and after every command, and passes its digest to the private input adapter for independent rechecks before exec. This is a point-in-time endpoint identity fence, not daemon attestation. It records durable intent before create, freezes full container configuration, verifies a single owner/CID/image/start generation, and rechecks source, input, material, tool and receipt. An uncertain create/start/configuration/generation leaves the CID retained for inspection. Only an exactly completed owned container is removed. Offline tests exercise file, exec and container fences with mocks; they are not evidence that Docker, mTLS, private FDs, or either architecture works.

The adapter tree is mounted as individual fixed read-only files: the exact 504 manifest source inventory, separately checked artifact and manifest, and two pinned module-tree inputs. No read-only `/adapter` ancestor bind is used; a nested bind target is rejected before create and during container inspection. Actual runtime compatibility still requires Root qualification.
